elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: New 11.4: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Commerce One shall ..." — covers both expiry and termination, for any reason.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: 11.4(a) provides assistance "for at least ninety (90) days"; there is no six-month (180-day) duration.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: No pricing basis appears in 11.4; the words "then-current rates" are absent.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: 11.4(b): "within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination, export and deliver to Corio all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Corio or its Customers."

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: 11.4(b) specifies no format; the phrase "commonly used, machine-readable format" (or equivalent) is missing.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No deletion-and-certification limb; retained 11.3 only requires return or destruction of Confidential Information with no written certification and no post-return sequencing.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: 11.4 trigger: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason" — both events covered, and the 90-day assistance period runs "following such expiration or termination" without any request/anticipation precondition.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: 11.4(a): "provide transition assistance to Corio for at least ninety (90) days following such expiration or termination." Vendor (Commerce One) is the obligor.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: 11.4(b): export and delivery "within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination" of "all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Corio or its Customers" — the deadline runs from termination, not from a request.

reasons: Finding status "missing" is correct: Sections 11.3 and 12 contain no exit-assistance or data-export mechanic; 11.3 addresses only survival, continued licence/support and mutual return or destruction of Confidential Information, and the escrow release conditions in Section 12 are not a data-return right.

Fallback is complete: all three fallback elements are satisfied by the single inserted Section 11.4 with an unconditional trigger on any expiration or termination, at least 90 days of Vendor assistance, and a 30-day export deadline anchored to expiry/termination rather than to a Customer request.

Preferred is not complete. To reach preferred the drafter must (i) extend 11.4(a) to "up to six (6) months", (ii) add "at Commerce One's then-current rates", (iii) add a format qualifier such as "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" to 11.4(b), and (iv) add a limb requiring Commerce One, after such return, to delete Corio's data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Minimal: the insertion adds only the two operative limbs needed for the fallback checklist, with no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no deletion/certification extras and no procedural boilerplate, and it deletes nothing from existing 11.3.

Preserves intent: retained 11.3 survival, Corio's continuing Customer licence and payment obligations, Commerce One's continuing support obligation, and the Confidential Information return/destroy carve-out all stand without contradiction; the new 11.4 numbering creates no dangling cross-reference or undefined term.
